stem: An application's CPU utilization rises and falls throughout the day in rough proportion to its request rate, with no fixed schedule and no known recurring pattern the team can point to. Which Auto Scaling policy should they configure?

choices.text: Scheduled scaling that changes capacity at fixed times of day
Target tracking that keeps average CPU utilization at a set value
Predictive scaling driven by machine learning over historical load
Step scaling that adjusts capacity in fixed amounts sized to alarm breaches

rationale: Target tracking keeps a chosen metric such as average CPU utilization at a set value and is the recommended default for variable traffic that moves roughly in proportion to load, exactly the pattern described. Scheduled scaling requires a known time to change capacity, but the team has no fixed schedule to act on. Predictive scaling forecasts capacity from a recurring historical pattern, but the team has no known recurring pattern to learn from. Step scaling is built to size its response to how far an alarm has been breached, which suits traffic that spikes in uneven jumps, not utilization that simply rises and falls in proportion to load.
